Listen to this article Share The Kano State Government has committed N37 billion towards settling outstanding gratuities and death benefits owed to retired civil servants and families of deceased public servants, while introducing monthly payments and digital verification to improve pension administration. Advertisement Advertisement Governor Abba Kabir Yusuf disclosed this during the distribution of the seventh tranche of N5 billion for the settlement of outstanding gratuities and death benefits at the Government House, Kano. The latest N5 billion disbursement brings the total amount committed by the administration to N37 billion, with the government setting April 2027 as its target for clearing all inherited pension liabilities. Yusuf said the administration inherited substantial unpaid gratuities, retirement benefits and death entitlements accumulated over several years, describing the failure to pay retirees their legitimate entitlements after decades of public service as an injustice. Read also: Kano moves to add 3,000 acres of irrigated farmland through dam projects He said the introduction of a dedicated monthly payment arrangement would replace the previous quarterly and intermittent disbursement system, assuring pensioners that payments would continue until all eligible beneficiaries received their entitlements. Advertisement The governor also announced the automation of the state’s monthly pension payroll and the completion of biometric data capture of pensioners as part of measures to improve transparency, accountability and efficiency. Under the new digital verification arrangement, pensioners living outside Kano, including those residing abroad, would be able to confirm their status remotely without travelling to the state. Advertisement He urged beneficiaries to download the Kano State Pension Fund Trustees Pensioner Verification Application from the Google Play Store to complete the verification process. Yusuf said the reforms were designed to strengthen pension administration, improve the management of beneficiaries’ records and minimise the difficulties associated with physical verification. Advertisement Advertisement He acknowledged that some retirees and families of deceased workers were still awaiting their entitlements but assured them that the government remained committed to clearing the outstanding liabilities by April 2027. According to him, the ongoing payments have provided financial relief to thousands of households, eased economic difficulties and helped restore the dignity of retired public servants and families of deceased workers. Read also: Kano seeks British investment to unlock economic potential, create jobs The governor commended the Kano State Pension Fund Trustees, the Office of the Head of Civil Service, the Ministry of Finance and the Nigeria Union of Pensioners, led by its president, Godwin Abumisi, for their contributions to the settlement programme and the implementation of the reforms. He also urged government officials responsible for the programme to ensure transparency, diligence and integrity in the monthly disbursement process. Yusuf further acknowledged recognition from the Association of Senior Civil Servants of Nigeria for his administration’s efforts towards addressing outstanding pension liabilities. He also appreciated the Correspondents’ Association of Nigeria for recognising him as its Friendly Governor of the Year 2026. The governor equally commended the Emir of Kano, Muhammadu Sanusi II, for his continued support for the welfare of senior citizens and the people of the state.
